58074-travels-into-bokhara-volume-1-of-3.creator: Unknown

arxiv-1710-06534.title: Lower Bounds for Numbers of Real Self-Dual Spaces in Problems of Schubert Calculus
arxiv-1710-06534.creator: Kang LU
arxiv-1710-06534.description: Abstract The self-dual spaces of polynomials are related to Bethe vectors in the Gaudin model associated to the Lie algebras of types B and C. In this paper, we give lower bounds for the numbers of real self-dual spaces in intersections of Schubert varieties related to osculating flags in the Grassmannian.

arxiv-2012-14429.title: Stability Conditions for the Horndeski Scalar Field Gravity Model
arxiv-2012-14429.creator: Cláudio Gomes, Orfeu Bertolami
arxiv-2012-14429.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Cláudio Gomes, Orfeu Bertolami. We constrain the viable models of Horndeski gravity, written in its equivalent Generalised Galileon version, by resorting to the Witten positive energy theorem. We find that the free function G 3 ​ ( ϕ , X ) G_{3}(\phi,X) in the Lagrangian is constrained to be a function solely of the scalar field, G 3 ​ ( ϕ ) G_{3}(\phi) , and relations among the free functions are found.

arxiv-2202-04296.title: A Projection-free Algorithm for Constrained Stochastic Multi-level Composition Optimization
arxiv-2202-04296.creator: Tesi Xiao, Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Saeed Ghadimi
arxiv-2202-04296.description: Abstract We propose a projection-free conditional gradient-type algorithm for smooth stochastic multi-level composition optimization, where the objective function is a nested composition of T T functions and the constraint set is a closed convex set. Our algorithm assumes access to noisy evaluations of the functions and their gradients, through a stochastic first-order oracle satisfying certain standard unbiasedness and second-moment assumptions.

arxiv-2301-05253.title: A Scalable Technique for Weak-Supervised Learning with Domain Constraints
arxiv-2301-05253.creator: Sudhir Agarwal, Anu Sreepathy, Lalla Mouatadid
arxiv-2301-05253.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sudhir Agarwal, Anu Sreepathy, Lalla Mouatadid. We propose a novel scalable end-to-end pipeline that uses symbolic domain knowledge as constraints for learning a neural network for classifying unlabeled data in a weak-supervised manner. Our approach is particularly well-suited for settings where the data consists of distinct groups (classes) that lends itself to clustering-friendly representation learning and the domain constraints can be reformulated for use of efficient mathematical optimization techniques by considering multiple training examples at once.

arxiv-2507-15339.title: LionGuard 2 : Building Lightweight, Data-Efficient & Localised Multilingual Content Moderators
arxiv-2507-15339.creator: Leanne Tan, Gabriel Chua, Ziyu Ge, Roy Ka-Wei Lee
arxiv-2507-15339.description: Abstract Modern moderation systems increasingly support multiple languages, but often fail to address localisation and low-resource variants - creating safety gaps in real-world deployments. Small models offer a potential alternative to large LLMs, yet still demand considerable data and compute.

arxiv-2508-03344.title: Stochastic systems with Bose-Hubbard interactions: Effects of bias on particles on a 𝟏 \mathbf{1} D lattice and random comb
arxiv-2508-03344.creator: Swastik Majumder 1,2, Mustansir Barma 1
arxiv-2508-03344.description: Abstract Driven non-equilibrium lattice models have wide-ranging applications in contexts such as mass transport, traffic flow, and transport in biological systems. In this work, we investigate the steady-state properties of a one-dimensional lattice system that allows multiple particle occupancy on each site. The particles undergo stochastic nearest-neighbor jumps influenced by both a directional bias and on-site repulsive interactions.

arxiv-2512-00494.title: Quantum Sensing via Large Spin-Clusters in Solid-State NMR: Optimal coherence order for practical sensing
arxiv-2512-00494.creator: C Alexander, T S Mahesh
arxiv-2512-00494.description: Abstract Quantum entanglement has long been recognized as an important resource for quantum sensing. In this work, we demonstrate the use of multiple-quantum solid-state NMR for quantum sensing by creating, manipulating, and detecting large clusters of correlated nuclear spins. We show that such clusters can sensitively detect pulse-width jitters in radio-frequency control fields at the level of tens of nanoseconds.

arxiv-2512-04731.title: Bridging Simulation and Reality: Cross-Domain Transfer with Semantic 2D Gaussian Splatting
arxiv-2512-04731.creator: Jian Tang, Pu Pang, Haowen Sun, Chengzhong Ma, Xingyu Chen, Hua Huang, Xuguang Lan
arxiv-2512-04731.description: Abstract Cross-domain transfer in robotic manipulation remains a longstanding challenge due to the significant domain gap between simulated and real-world environments. Existing methods such as domain randomization, adaptation, and sim-real calibration often require extensive tuning or fail to generalize to unseen scenarios.

arxiv-2605-11244.creator: Alexander Pigazzini

pmc-11305031.title: Assessing the prevalence of obesity in a Russian adult population by six indices and their associations with hypertension, diabetes mellitus and hypercholesterolaemia
pmc-11305031.creator: Kamila Kholmatova, Alexandra Krettek, Irina V Dvoryashina, Sofia Malyutina, Alexander V Kudryavtsev
pmc-11305031.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The anthropometric index that best predicts cardiometabolic risk remains inconclusive. This study therefore assessed the prevalence of obesity using six indices and compared their associations with obesity-related cardiometabolic disorders. We determined obesity prevalence according to body mass index, waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), body fat percentage and fat mass index (FMI) using data from the Know Your Heart study (n = 4495, 35–69 years).

pmc-11328603.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of (thio)urea derivatives as potent Escherichia coli β-glucuronidase inhibitors
pmc-11328603.creator: Keren Xu, Leyi Ying, Titi Ying, Qihao Wu, Lin Du, Yanlei Yu, Youmin Ying, Bin Wei, Hong Wang, Zhikun Yang
pmc-11328603.description: EcGUS has drawn considerable attention for its role as a target in alleviating serious GIAEs. In this study, a series of 72 (thio)urea derivatives were designed, synthesised, and biologically assayed. The bioassay results revealed that E-9 (IC50 = 2.68 μM) exhibited a promising inhibitory effect on EcGUS, surpassing EcGUS inhibitor D-saccharic acid-1,4-lactone (DSL, IC50 = 45.8 μM).

pmc-11493150.title: Neurocognitive functioning during adolescence: Spanish validation of the Penn Computerized Neurocognitive Battery
pmc-11493150.creator: Xacobe Fernández‐García, Félix Inchausti, Alicia Pérez‐Albéniz, Javier Ortuño‐Sierra, Raquel Falcó, Eduardo Fonseca‐Pedrero
pmc-11493150.description: ObjectivesThe Penn Computerized Neurocognitive Battery ‐ Child Version (PennCNB‐cv) is presented as a brief tool that allows comprehensive and automated assessment of 5 factors (via 14 performance tasks): Executive Control, Episodic Memory, Complex Cognition, Social Cognition, and Sensorimotor Speed. The literature links (dys)functions in these areas with psycho(patho)logical constructs, but evidence is scarce among Spanish‐speaking youth.

pmc-11517751.title: Inclusion of Long Covid patients in the care trajectory post-Covid-19: evidence from Belgium
pmc-11517751.creator: S Moreels, R De Schreye, S Bensemmane
pmc-11517751.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundEvidence suggests that 10-30% of COVID-19 infected people develop persistent symptoms that can be diagnosed as Long Covid. Most Long Covid cases are in patients with a mild acute COVID-19 infection and are mainly treated in primary health care. In July 2022, a care trajectory (CT) post-Covid-19 was launched in Belgium, in which Long Covid patients can benefit from reimbursement of treatment costs when consulting health professionals in primary health care for their rehabilitation.

pmc-11518835.title: Nationwide usage of ethambutol and incidence and screening practices of optic neuropathy
pmc-11518835.creator: Jiyeong Kim, Hyeon Yoon Kwon, Seong Joon Ahn
pmc-11518835.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionEthambutol, a key anti-tuberculosis medication, is associated with optic neuropathy, which can lead to significant vision impairment. This population-based cohort study investigated the nationwide usage of ethambutol and the incidence and screening of optic neuropathy among ethambutol users.MethodsThe cohort included 206,157 individuals from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment database in South Korea who initiated ethambutol therapy between 1 January 2015, and 31 December 2021. Among them, 117,309 individuals without prior ophthalmic diseases were analyzed to investigate practice patterns.

pmc-11696605.title: Awareness and acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccine in the Middle East: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression of 159 studies
pmc-11696605.creator: Bugra Taygun Gulle, Pinar Kiran, Saadet Goksu Celik, Zeynep Sedef Varol, Neslisah Siyve, Ahmet Naci Emecen, Hilal Duzel
pmc-11696605.description: Cervical cancer, closely linked to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, is a major global health concern. Our study aims to fill the gap in understanding HPV vaccine awareness and acceptance in the Middle East, where national immunization programs are often lacking and cultural perceptions hinder acceptance.

pmc-12953903.title: The dynamic distribution of genetic tandem amplifications in a heteroresistant Escherichia coli population revealed by ultra-deep long read sequencing
pmc-12953903.creator: Sofia Jonsson, Andrei Guliaev, Brandon A Berryhill, Dan I Andersson, Hervé Nicoloff
pmc-12953903.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Antibiotic heteroresistance, characterized by rare resistant subpopulations of bacteria within a susceptible main population, is associated with treatment failure and often caused by tandem amplification of resistance genes. Here, we investigated how the distribution of tandem amplifications affects heteroresistance using an approach combining genetic engineering and ultra-deep Nanopore sequencing to accurately quantify the distribution of tandem amplification copy numbers on plasmids down to frequencies of 10-5.

pmc-12999538.title: Simultaneous measurement of water transport across the blood–brain and blood–CSF barrier in the human brain with arterial spin labeling MRI
pmc-12999538.creator: Léonie Petitclerc, Helena Durrant, Lydiane Hirschler, Lena Václavů, Matthias JP van Osch
pmc-12999538.description: Previously, water exchange across the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and blood–cerebrospinal barrier (BCSFB) was assessed by multi-delay, multi-echotime (TE) arterial spin labeling, albeit in separate acquisitions with different settings. In this study, we present a protocol for simultaneous measurement of BBB and BCSFB water exchange using a multi-TE 3D-GRASE acquisition combined with T2-preparation.

pmc-13156581.title: Unilateral agenesis of the right cerebellar hemisphere in a child: When one hemisphere is missing, the brain adapts
pmc-13156581.creator: Hind Qajia, Saleck Choumad, Fadwa El Bakari, Yassine Eddahoumi, Nazik Allali, Latifa Chat, Siham El Haddad
pmc-13156581.description: Unilateral agenesis of the cerebellar hemisphere is a rare congenital anomaly, typically revealed by psychomotor delay or motor difficulties in children. We report the case of a 5-year-old boy who presented with psychomotor delay, in whom magnetic resonance imaging revealed agenesis of the right cerebellar hemisphere associated with vermian hypoplasia.

pmc-13233479.title: Efficacy and safety of anisodine hydrobromide injection in acute ischemic stroke—a multicenter real-world observational study
pmc-13233479.creator: Tianxiang Lan, Yajun Cheng, Tang Yang, Yuying Yan, Jingyu Cui, Shuai Jiang, Bo Wu
pmc-13233479.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the efficacy and safety of anisodine hydrobromide injection in patients with acute ischemic stroke in a real-world clinical setting.DesignMulticenter, real-world observational cohort study conducted from April 2018 to December 2021 with 90-day follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were applied.

pmc-13366698.title: Cipepofol for adjunctive sedation during neuraxial anesthesia: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13366698.creator: Mi Chen, Lirong Chen, Yang Yang, Shuhua Huang, Yimin Ren, Lin Wang
pmc-13366698.description: BackgroundCipepofol is a novel 2,6-disubstituted phenol derivative increasingly used for anesthesia and sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy and fiberoptic bronchoscopy. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of cipepofol for adjunctive sedation during neuraxial anesthesia, thereby providing evidence for its clinical application.MethodsThis was a randomized, double-blind, non-inferiority trial.

pmc-13457783.title: Clinically Silent Presentation of Acalculous Gangrenous Cholecystitis: A Case Report
pmc-13457783.creator: Ia Mikadze, Elene Saribekovi, Elene Pachkoria, Tamar Didbaridze, Tamar Megrelishvili, Teimuraz Goletiani, George Burkadze, Salome Lobzhanidze, Magda Rurua, Emzar Pipia, Levan Ratiani
pmc-13457783.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acalculous gangrenous cholecystitis is a rare, life-threatening form of acute cholecystitis associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Neurological deficits may obscure early recognition of severe intra-abdominal pathology, contributing to delayed diagnosis and potentially worse clinical outcomes.We report a case of a 43-year-old male with recent intracerebral hemorrhage and residual right-sided hemiplegia who presented with high-grade fever and progressive clinical deterioration without prominent abdominal findings. Laboratory investigations demonstrated pronounced inflammatory changes accompanied by a predominantly cholestatic pattern of liver enzyme abnormalities.

pmc-13632054.title: Restoring the lost heat of the joint: Thermomechanical stimulation as a candidate treatment for early-stage osteoarthritis
pmc-13632054.creator: Antoine Reitzel, Deniz Cemre Turgut, Céline Samira Wyss, Vincent Stadelmann, Dominique P. Pioletti
pmc-13632054.description: Two of the oldest osteoarthritis treatments, local heat and therapeutic exercise, have evolved along separate paths: heat as a symptomatic adjunct and exercise as a functional intervention. Neither intervention alone modifies the disease. This separation reflects clinical tradition, not joint physiology. Articular cartilage dissipates some of the energy absorbed during deformation.
